items.explanation: 48-year-old man; paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is documented in the problem list of serial cardiology clinic notes from 19 Jul 2025 through 12 Jun 2026. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure documented Feb 2025 admission - acute systolic heart failure/cardiomyopathy; unspecified essential hypertension); age <65, no diabetes, stroke/TIA, vascular disease, and male. With a score of 2 in a man the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation, but no anticoagulant order is active as of 2026-09-24 12:00 (current orders: famotidine, pantoprazole).

Most recent ECG (10 Nov 2023, 104821039): sinus rhythm 70 bpm, QT 506 ms, RR 0.86 s, Bazett QTc 547 ms (up from 417 ms on the 17 Jun 2020 tracing) - above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. The patient is on citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list), re-ordered 29 May 2026 and current to 25 Dec 2026; 40 mg also exceeds the 20 mg/day maximum recommended for QT reasons. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (21 Jan 2026) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (1 Dec 2023) are normal. Prescriber review required.

Most recent ECG (8 Oct 2023, 108018814): sinus rhythm 68 bpm, QT 487 ms, RR 0.88 s, Bazett QTc 520 ms - above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo (and markedly increased from QTc 357 ms on 23 Nov 2022). Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the 14 May 2024 visit on the basis of that same tracing, which the note described as 'QT acceptable'; the order of 23 Apr 2026 is current to 2 Jan 2027. Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (both 23 Aug 2025) are normal. Prescriber review and a repeat ECG are required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the 10 Nov 2025 Cardiology Clinic visit. Because the start pre-dates 1 Mar 2026 the 1 Sep 2025 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 10 Dec 2025. A 12-lead ECG (106885519) was obtained on 24 Nov 2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met. (That ECG showed QTc 535 ms, which is handled as a separate QT-safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the 12 Feb 2026 Cardiology Clinic visit. The start pre-dates 1 Mar 2026, so the 30-day window of the 1 Sep 2025 memo applies (the 1 Mar 2026 revision explicitly leaves earlier starts on 30 days): ECG due by 14 Mar 2026. A 12-lead ECG (101538691) was recorded on 8 Mar 2026, 24 days after the start - requirement met. QTc on that tracing was 477 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the 2 Mar 2026 Cardiology Clinic visit (order authored 2 Mar 2026 13:55 and listed as a current medication in that day's note). Because the start is on/after 1 Mar 2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 16 Mar 2026. A 12-lead ECG (104882441) was obtained on 7 Mar 2026 - requirement met; it showed sinus rhythm with QTc 379 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the 10 Apr 2026 Cardiology Clinic visit, so under the revised memo an ECG was required within 14 days, by 24 Apr 2026. No ECG exists in that window; the only tracing for this patient (107859369) was recorded on 29 Apr 2026, five days after the deadline, so the requirement was not satisfied within the required time and is overdue. (The late ECG showed sinus rhythm 70 bpm, QTc 380 ms.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the 1 Aug 2026 Cardiology Clinic visit; under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 15 Aug 2026. The patient's only ECG in the chart is 106035722 from 25 Dec 2025, well before the drug was started, and no ECG has been obtained since. The deadline has passed, so the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the 10 Aug 2026 Cardiology Clinic visit; under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 24 Aug 2026. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, but the 25 Aug 2026 telephone note records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 18 Aug 2026 - inside the required window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the 15 Sep 2026 Cardiology Clinic visit; under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 29 Sep 2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (the most recent tracing is 104253928 from 9 Mar 2025), but the deadline falls after the 24 Sep 2026 evaluation time, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the 1 Sep 2026 Cardiology Clinic visit Dr Kessler documented 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' - a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician, so the 1 Mar 2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days, by 8 Sep 2026. An INR(PT) of 2.3 was resulted on 5 Sep 2026, four days after the change, so the requirement was met.

80-year-old woman; persistent atrial fibrillation is carried in the problem list of every cardiology clinic note from 12 Sep 2025 to 28 May 2026. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: congestive heart failure (I50.40/I50.43/I110), hypertension, age 80 (2 points), type 2 diabetes (E11.649), prior cerebral infarction/TIA with residual deficits (Z86.73 history of TIA, I69.3x sequelae) (2 points), vascular disease (old myocardial infarction, coronary atherosclerosis), female sex. Anticoagulation is strongly recommended, but the only active orders on 2026-09-24 are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg - no anticoagulant.

The 10 Sep 2026 anticoagulation-clinic note by L. Nguyen, PharmD records a home INR of 3.4 and 'warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol' - a dose change by a clinic pharmacist acting under the anticoagulation standing order, so the 1 Mar 2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days, by 17 Sep 2026. The most recent INR(PT) in the chart is 2.6 from 22 Aug 2026, i.e. before the change, and no INR has been drawn since. The due date has passed, so the follow-up INR is overdue.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (ICD-9 427.31, coded 22 Aug 2025) that is also carried in the cardiology clinic problem list through 28 Jul 2026. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (unspecified essential hypertension; age 71 = 1 point for 65-74; vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery). No heart failure, diabetes or prior stroke/TIA. Guideline recommends oral anticoagulation; the only active medication order on 2026-09-24 is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, with no anticoagulant ever prescribed in the clinic record.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (I48.0) coded 14 Mar 2025 during the admission for cardioembolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: hypertension, age 71 (1 point), prior ischaemic stroke (I63.40 cerebral infarction due to embolism, with residual hemiplegia I69.35/I69.39) (2 points), female sex. Guideline recommends oral anticoagulation, and the stroke was embolic; nevertheless the current clinic orders (10 Jul 2026) are carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine only, with no anticoagulant. Her 14 Mar 2025 ECG showed sinus rhythm with a single premature beat, which does not remove the indication in paroxysmal AF.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered on 20 Aug 2026 (valid to 28 Dec 2026) and is listed as a current medication in the 20 Aug 2026 clinic note, despite the 12 Aug 2026 outside-records summary documenting a 2-5 Aug 2026 admission to Mercy Hospital for upper gastrointestinal bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly HELD AT DISCHARGE PENDING CARDIOLOGY REVIEW. The patient is also on aspirin and clopidogrel, compounding bleeding risk. There is no documented cardiology review authorising resumption, so continuation of apixaban needs prescriber review.

Two direct oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current. At the 15 Jul 2026 cardiology visit the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban prescription was re-issued the same day (rivaroxaban 20 mg daily, 15 Jul 2026 - 25 Dec 2026) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily (15 Jul 2026 - 26 Dec 2026), and the note's medication list itself shows both drugs. Both orders are still valid on 2026-09-24, giving overlapping full-dose anticoagulation in a patient with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

The 10 Jun 2026 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves at a mean ventricular rate of 132 and 136 bpm respectively (RR 0.35-0.72 s, RMSSD 116 ms / 98 ms) - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72 bpm. An unspecified atrial fibrillation diagnosis (I48.91) was in fact coded for the same encounter, so the narrative rhythm statement contradicts the tracing and needs correction/review.

Most recent ECG (24 Nov 2025, 106885519): sinus rhythm 62 bpm, QT 526 ms, RR 0.97 s, Bazett QTc 535 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. The patient takes amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list), most recently re-ordered 29 Jul 2026 and current through 5 Jan 2027, together with warfarin. Most recent electrolytes are normal (potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL, both 20 Apr 2026), so the prolongation is not explained by hypokalaemia or hypomagnesaemia. Prescriber review required.

Most recent ECG (27 Apr 2022, 101515306) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT 559 ms and RR 1.04 s, giving a Bazett QTc of 547 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. This 95-year-old woman remains on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list; order of 22 Aug 2026 current to 5 Jan 2027) plus warfarin and metoprolol. Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (both 14 Feb 2026) are within normal limits. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a repeat ECG are required.

interpretations.explanation: 23 Nov 2025. Regular narrow-complex rhythm, RR 0.79-0.92 s (mean 72 bpm), uniform upright P waves in II/aVF preceding every QRS (P-wave template correlation 0.98) with PR 172 ms - normal sinus rhythm. QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block pattern (rS in V1, dominant R in V6). Frontal axis +11 degrees (normal). QT 357 ms at RR 0.82 s gives Bazett QTc 394 ms, a fall of about 140 ms from the QTc of 535 ms on the 21 Nov 2025 tracing, so QTC_DECREASE_60. The same-day clinic note describing sinus rhythm is consistent with this ECG.

23 May 2024, the only ECG for this patient. Regular rhythm at 98 bpm (RR 0.60-0.63 s); a P wave runs from about -148 to -84 ms in II/III/aVF and is followed by a short isoelectric PR segment, PR 118 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +4 degrees (normal). QT 309 ms at RR 0.62 s gives QTc 393 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

17 Sep 2024, the only ECG for this patient. Irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm: RR intervals range 0.39-1.09 s with RMSSD 265 ms and 73 per cent of successive RR differences over 60 ms, and there is no reproducible P wave before the QRS complexes (P-template correlation 0.38, amplitude at noise level) - atrial fibrillation, mean ventricular rate 101 bpm. No measurable PR interval. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis -53 degrees (left axis deviation). QT 329 ms at median RR 0.61 s gives QTc 422 ms. No prior tracing. This confirms the coded atrial fibrillation for which the patient receives warfarin.

13 Jan 2019. Regular rhythm at 53 bpm (RR 1.11-1.17 s) with consistent P waves and PR 146 ms - sinus bradycardia. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block (the 13 Dec 2018 tracing had a slightly wider QRS of about 106 ms but still below 120 ms, so no resolved block). Axis -5 degrees. QTc (Bazett) 363 ms versus 387 ms previously - no qualifying change.

27 Apr 2022. Regular rhythm at 58 bpm (RR 0.97-1.10 s, RMSSD 36 ms) with a low-amplitude but reproducible P wave about 200 ms before each QRS, PR 166 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +38 degrees. QT is very long at 559 ms with RR 1.04 s, Bazett QTc 547 ms. The previous tracing (6 Apr 2022) showed irregularly irregular RR 0.32-0.62 s with absent P waves at 130 bpm - atrial fibrillation - so there is RESOLVED_AF, and the QTc has risen from 455 to 547 ms, giving QTC_INCREASE_60. She remains on amiodarone; the prolonged QTc is raised separately as a QT-safety item.

8 Oct 2023. Regular rhythm at 68 bpm (RR 0.86-0.90 s) with 1:1 P waves and PR 132 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +44 degrees. QT 487 ms at RR 0.88 s gives Bazett QTc 520 ms, up from 357 ms on 23 Nov 2022 - QTC_INCREASE_60. Escitalopram was subsequently started on the basis of this tracing being reported as 'QT acceptable', which the measurement does not support; the prolonged QTc on watch-list therapy is filed as a separate QT-safety item.

23 Aug 2025, the only ECG for this patient. Regular rhythm at 83 bpm (RR 0.72-0.73 s) with uniform P waves and PR 154 ms - normal sinus rhythm. QRS 74 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +54 degrees. QT 347 ms at RR 0.72 s gives QTc 409 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

13 Jul 2022. Regular rhythm at 141 bpm (RR 0.40-0.45 s, RMSSD 11 ms). A single reproducible atrial deflection precedes each QRS at about -170 to -130 ms, followed by a truly isoelectric PR segment, and the TP segment is flat - sinus tachycardia rather than 2:1 atrial flutter or fibrillation. PR about 132 ms, QRS 76 ms with deep S in V1-V2 (no bundle branch block), axis about 0 degrees. QT 248 ms at RR 0.43 s gives QTc 380 ms. The 11 Jul 2022 tracing was irregularly irregular (RR 0.38-0.82 s, RMSSD 190 ms) with no P waves - atrial fibrillation - so RESOLVED_AF. QTc change (430 to 380 ms) is under 60 ms. Despite an implanted pacemaker there is no pacing spike or paced morphology on this tracing.

19 Mar 2025. Regular rhythm at 102 bpm (RR 0.58-0.60 s) with reproducible P waves and PR 146 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +46 degrees. Shallow T-wave inversion inferolaterally. QTc (Bazett) 431 ms versus 427 ms on the 18 Mar 2025 tracing - no change.

10 Jun 2026 19:36. Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia: RR 0.35-0.65 s, RMSSD 98 ms, half of successive RR differences over 60 ms, and no organised P wave anywhere before the QRS complexes (P-template correlation 0.11, amplitude 0.03 mV at noise level) - atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of 136 bpm. No measurable PR interval. QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -2 degrees. QT 282 ms at median RR 0.42 s gives Bazett QTc 436 ms. The earlier tracing the same afternoon (107914094, 17:13) was also atrial fibrillation at 132 bpm with QTc 439 ms, so no change. Note the same-day clinic note reports 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which this tracing contradicts (raised as a separate review item).

18 Jan 2021. Regular rhythm at 120 bpm (RR 0.49-0.50 s) with a P wave before every QRS and PR 172 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +51 degrees. QT 273 ms at RR 0.50 s gives QTc 387 ms, essentially unchanged from 392 ms on 16 Sep 2016. No changes.

16 Jul 2022. Regular rhythm at 91 bpm (RR 0.65-0.67 s) with consistent P waves and PR 148 ms - sinus rhythm. Narrow QRS 74 ms, no conduction block. Axis -17 degrees (normal). QTc (Bazett) 408 ms, essentially unchanged from 390 ms on the previous tracing (16 May 2021); no new rhythm, block or QTc change.

2 Aug 2025. Regular rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 0.86-0.88 s) with reproducible P waves and PR 136 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis -25 degrees (within normal limits). QT 411 ms at RR 0.87 s gives QTc 441 ms versus 407 ms on 27 Apr 2025 - a rise of 34 ms, below the 60 ms threshold. No rhythm or conduction change.

29 Apr 2026, the only ECG for this patient. Regular rhythm at 70 bpm (RR 0.84-0.88 s) with a reproducible atrial deflection from about -190 to -115 ms preceding every QRS and an isoelectric PR segment, PR about 145 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block. The limb leads are strikingly discordant: lead I and aVL are almost entirely negative (S 1.4 and 0.9 mV) while aVR shows a tall positive R and lead III a dominant R, giving a computed frontal axis of about -172 degrees, i.e. an extreme (north-west) axis; right/left arm lead reversal should be excluded before accepting this as a true axis. QT 354 ms at RR 0.87 s gives QTc 380 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

15 Nov 2024. Irregularly irregular rhythm: RR intervals 0.69, 0.73, 0.74, 0.91, 1.13, 1.13, 1.15, 1.15, 1.16 s (RMSSD 288 ms, 62 per cent of successive differences over 60 ms) with no reproducible P wave (template correlation 0.19) - atrial fibrillation, mean ventricular rate 61 bpm, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +28 degrees. QT 456 ms at median RR 1.13 s gives QTc 429 ms. The 12 Nov 2024 tracing showed regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear P waves and PR 166 ms, so this is NEW_AF; QTc change (405 to 429 ms) is under 60 ms.

8 Mar 2026, the only ECG for this patient, obtained as the post-escitalopram monitoring study. Regular rhythm at 68 bpm (RR 0.86-0.91 s) with clear P waves and PR 128 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +62 degrees. QT 447 ms at RR 0.88 s gives Bazett QTc 477 ms - borderline prolonged but below the 500 ms clinic review threshold. No prior tracing for comparison.

15 Feb 2025, the only ECG for this patient. Regular rhythm at 74 bpm (RR 0.78-0.84 s) with a P wave before every QRS and PR 186 ms - sinus rhythm with normal (upper-normal) AV conduction, below the 200 ms first-degree block threshold. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +55 degrees. QT 380 ms at RR 0.81 s gives QTc 422 ms. No prior ECG.

5 Dec 2024 14:38. Regular rhythm at 122 bpm (RR 0.49-0.50 s, RMSSD 2 ms) with a small reproducible P wave (template correlation 0.99) and PR about 110 ms - sinus tachycardia. Low-voltage QRS of 90 ms with rS/RS complexes throughout and no terminal R' in V1, so no bundle branch block; net QRS is negative in lead I with a slightly positive aVF, giving a frontal axis near +145 degrees (right axis deviation). QT 290 ms at RR 0.49 s gives QTc 413 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (106516875, 01:33) showed a QRS of about 135 ms with a tall terminal R' in V1 and terminal S in I - right bundle branch block, matching the RBBB coded for that admission - which is no longer present, hence RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK. QTc change (452 to 413 ms) is under 60 ms.

13 Sep 2025 07:17. Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia, RR 0.29-0.58 s (RMSSD 104 ms, 52 per cent of successive differences over 60 ms), with no organised atrial activity - the pre-QRS segment is different on every beat (P-template correlation 0.08) - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate 151 bpm; no measurable PR interval. QRS 68 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -12 degrees. QT 260 ms at median RR 0.39 s gives QTc 414 ms. The 12 Sep 2025 tracing was sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with PR 158 ms (a single premature beat accounting for its RR variability), so this is NEW_AF. QTc is unchanged (412 to 414 ms).

7 Mar 2026, the only ECG for this patient, obtained five days after citalopram was started. Rhythm is regular apart from mild variation (RR 0.66-0.86 s) with a uniform upright P wave in II/aVF before every QRS (template correlation 0.97) and PR 156 ms - sinus rhythm at a mean 81 bpm. QRS 80 ms, rS in V1 and dominant R in V6, no bundle branch block; axis +47 degrees. QT 327 ms at median RR 0.74 s gives Bazett QTc 379 ms, well below the 500 ms threshold. No prior tracing. The same-day note reporting sinus rhythm is consistent with this ECG.

10 Nov 2023. Regular rhythm at 70 bpm (RR 0.80-0.89 s) with reproducible P waves and PR 162 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 102 ms, below the 120 ms bundle branch block threshold; axis +38 degrees. QT 506 ms at RR 0.86 s gives Bazett QTc 547 ms, a rise from 417 ms on the 17 Jun 2020 tracing - QTC_INCREASE_60. She takes citalopram 40 mg daily, so the prolonged QTc is also raised as a QT-safety item.

22 Sep 2025, the only ECG for this patient. Regular rhythm at 66 bpm (RR 0.90-0.93 s) with a P wave before each QRS and PR 120 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 94 ms with low precordial voltages but no bundle branch block pattern; axis -20 degrees (normal). QT 370 ms at RR 0.91 s gives QTc 388 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

15 Jul 2025. Regular rhythm at 104 bpm (RR 0.57-0.59 s) with a consistent upright P wave in II/aVF (PR about 138 ms) - sinus tachycardia. QRS 98 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6, no bundle branch block. Axis +39 degrees (normal). QT 368 ms at RR 0.58 s gives QTc 483 ms - borderline prolonged but below the 500 ms clinic threshold, and within 60 ms of the 457 ms on the 20 Jun 2025 tracing, which was also sinus. No qualifying interval change.

9 Mar 2025. Regular rhythm at 58 bpm (RR 0.98-1.08 s) with a biphasic P wave from about -158 to -84 ms before every QRS and PR 118 ms - sinus bradycardia. QRS 86 ms, deep S in V1 with dominant R in V6, no bundle branch block; axis +61 degrees. QT 422 ms at RR 1.03 s gives QTc 416 ms versus 438 ms on the 8 Mar 2025 tracing - no qualifying change. This is the most recent ECG and pre-dates the haloperidol started on 15 Sep 2026, for which monitoring is not yet due.

12 May 2025, the only ECG for this patient. Regular rhythm at 82 bpm (RR 0.71-0.74 s) with uniform P waves (template correlation 0.98) and PR 142 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 96 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +34 degrees. QT 374 ms at RR 0.73 s gives QTc 439 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

1 May 2022. Regular rhythm at 107 bpm (RR 0.55-0.56 s, RMSSD 3 ms) with a reproducible P wave and PR 126 ms - sinus tachycardia; there is no sawtooth flutter baseline and the atrial-to-ventricular relationship is 1:1. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +56 degrees. QT 325 ms at RR 0.56 s gives QTc 434 ms, essentially unchanged from 428 ms on 27 Jul 2019. No changes.

17 Jul 2024. Rhythm is sinus at a mean 59 bpm (RR 0.95-1.20 s) with a P wave before each QRS and PR 180 ms. The QRS is broad at 132 ms with a broad monophasic R in I, aVL and V6 and a wide deep S in V1-V2 with no septal q waves - left bundle branch block. Frontal axis -21 degrees (within normal limits). QT 447 ms at RR 0.98 s gives QTc 451 ms. The 3 Jun 2024 tracing showed the identical 132 ms LBBB pattern with QTc 462 ms, so the block is not new and there is no qualifying QTc change. No pacing spikes are present.

21 May 2024, the only ECG for this patient. Regular rhythm at 108 bpm (RR 0.54-0.62 s) with reproducible P waves and PR 116 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees. QT 341 ms at RR 0.55 s gives Bazett QTc 461 ms (Bazett over-corrects at this rate); below the 500 ms threshold. No prior tracing for comparison.

19 Jun 2020. Regular rhythm at 76 bpm (RR 0.77-0.80 s) with prominent uniform P waves and PR 138 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 68 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +64 degrees. QT 406 ms at RR 0.78 s gives QTc 459 ms, compared with 503 ms on the 2 Feb 2020 tracing - a fall of 44 ms, below the 60 ms threshold, so no change is reported.

25 Dec 2025, the only ECG for this patient. Regular rhythm at 72 bpm (RR 0.82-0.84 s) with a P wave before every QRS and PR 144 ms - normal sinus rhythm. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +22 degrees. QT 382 ms at RR 0.83 s gives QTc 419 ms. No prior tracing. This ECG pre-dates the escitalopram started 1 Aug 2026, so it does not satisfy the post-start monitoring requirement (filed separately).

14 Mar 2025, the only ECG for this patient. The underlying rhythm is sinus at a mean 62 bpm: RR intervals are 0.98, 0.99, 1.00, 0.97, 0.96, 0.96, 0.98 s with a single early beat (0.54 s) and compensatory pause (1.37 s) - one premature complex, not the irregular irregularity of atrial fibrillation, and a reproducible P wave (about -255 to -140 ms) precedes each sinus beat. PR measures about 204 ms, just beyond the 200 ms limit, so first-degree AV block. QRS 102 ms, below the bundle branch block threshold; frontal axis about -32 degrees (borderline left axis deviation). QT 388 ms at median RR 0.98 s gives QTc 392 ms. No prior tracing for comparison. Note that sinus rhythm on this single tracing does not exclude the coded paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

24 Nov 2025. Regular rhythm at 62 bpm (RR 0.94-0.98 s), P wave before each QRS with PR 168 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 98 ms with no bundle branch block. Axis +67 degrees (normal). QT is markedly long at 526 ms with RR 0.97 s, Bazett QTc 535 ms, up from 413 ms on the 7 Jun 2025 tracing - QTC_INCREASE_60. The prior ECG showed sinus bradycardia at 49 bpm with marked sinus arrhythmia, not atrial fibrillation, so there is no rhythm change. Amiodarone was started two weeks before this tracing; marked QT prolongation is flagged separately as a QT-safety item.

26 Jun 2023. Perfectly regular rhythm at 112 bpm (RR 0.54 s) with a discrete P wave from -200 to -130 ms, an isoelectric PR segment and PR 166 ms - sinus tachycardia, not atrial flutter (no sawtooth, single atrial deflection per cycle, isoelectric TP segment). QRS 94 ms; deep S in V1-V2 with tall R in V5-V6 but no bundle branch block. Axis +35 degrees. QTc (Bazett) 391 ms, unchanged from 387 ms on 4 Jul 2022. No changes.

24 Oct 2024. Regular rhythm at 52 bpm (RR 1.14-1.18 s) with 1:1 P waves and PR 168 ms - sinus bradycardia. QRS 92 ms, high-voltage R in V5-V6, no bundle branch block. Axis +36 degrees. QTc (Bazett) 400 ms versus 390 ms on the 22 May 2023 tracing (which showed sinus rhythm with intermittently dropped beats consistent with the documented Mobitz II block) - no qualifying change. AV conduction is 1:1 with a normal PR on this tracing.

23 Jun 2025. Regular rhythm at 55 bpm (RR 1.07-1.12 s). A broad P wave runs from about -256 to -170 ms and is followed by a long isoelectric PR segment; PR measures 220 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block (also present, at 196-200 ms, on the 30 Nov 2024 tracing). QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +4 degrees. Tall peaked T waves; QT 398 ms at RR 1.10 s gives QTc 379 ms, unchanged from 361 ms previously. No rhythm or QTc change.

19 Apr 2024, the only ECG for this patient. Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 121 bpm (RR 0.49-0.50 s) with a P wave preceding every QRS and PR 118 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +67 degrees (normal). QT 294 ms at RR 0.50 s gives Bazett QTc 417 ms. No prior tracing, so no comparison is possible.

23 Aug 2021 10:07, a repeat taken 34 seconds after the 10:06 tracing. Regular rhythm at 102 bpm with uniform P waves and PR 148 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 90 ms, rS in V1, no bundle branch block; axis +59 degrees. QTc (Bazett) 421 ms, identical to the 414 ms of the immediately preceding tracing. No changes.

arguments.explanation: 14 Mar 2025, the only ECG for this patient. The underlying rhythm is sinus at a mean 62 bpm: RR intervals are 0.98, 0.99, 1.00, 0.97, 0.96, 0.96, 0.98 s with a single early beat (0.54 s) and compensatory pause (1.37 s) - one premature complex, not the irregular irregularity of atrial fibrillation, and a reproducible P wave (about -255 to -140 ms) precedes each sinus beat. PR measures about 204 ms, just beyond the 200 ms limit, so first-degree AV block. QRS 102 ms, below the bundle branch block threshold; frontal axis about -32 degrees (borderline left axis deviation). QT 388 ms at median RR 0.98 s gives QTc 392 ms. No prior tracing for comparison. Note that sinus rhythm on this single tracing does not exclude the coded paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

The same-day clinic note describing sinus rhythm is consistent with this ECG.

No measurable PR interval. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis -53 degrees (left axis deviation). QT 329 ms at median RR 0.61 s gives QTc 422 ms. No prior tracing. This confirms the coded atrial fibrillation for which the patient receives warfarin.

QTc (Bazett) 363 ms versus 387 ms previously - no qualifying change.

This confirms the coded atrial fibrillation for which the patient receives warfarin.

QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block (the 13 Dec 2018 tracing had a slightly wider QRS of about 106 ms but still below 120 ms, so no resolved block). Axis -5 degrees. QTc (Bazett) 363 ms versus 387 ms previously - no qualifying change.
